tip: Months take i: i december = in December, i juli = in July.
The verb keeps second place even when another word leads: September börjar hösten.
With åka, transport takes no article: åker spårvagn = take the tram, åker buss = take the bus.
Jobs drop the article after är: Hon är läkare, not en läkare.
The -s ending makes it passive: laddas = is being charged, from ladda = to charge.
känna sig means feel; the reflexive mig matches jag: känner mig trött.
titta always takes på for what you watch: tittar på TV.
en-words use min: min syster, min bil. Mitt is for ett-words.
ett-words use mitt: mitt hus. En-words use min instead.
Weather uses det as a placeholder subject: Det är kallt = it is cold.
på marks being at a place like a library: på biblioteket.
lägger mig literally lays myself down, the everyday way to say go to bed.
börja takes a plain infinitive, no att: börjar jobba = start to work.
Floors use på plus an ordinal: på tredje våningen = on the third floor.
this = den här plus the noun in its definite form: den här veckan = this week.
Det tar plus a time plus att plus verb = it takes that long to: tar tre timmar att köra.
att = that, linking the thought to tror: tror att det blir regn.
tycker om = like; om is a fixed particle you cannot drop: tycker om att promenera.
på plus a plural weekday means every one: på lördagar = on Saturdays, every Saturday.
Swedish has no word for of here: en kopp te = a cup of tea, just place the words together.
vår becomes våra before a plural noun: våra föräldrar = our parents.
Add -s for measurement: fem minuters promenad = a five-minute walk.
Many en-words add -ar in the plural: en hund, två hundar.
Adjectives add -a when the subject is plural: barnen är trötta.
i marks how long something lasts: i en timme = for an hour.
-or plural nouns end in -orna when definite: blommor becomes blommorna = the flowers.
ska plus an infinitive expresses the future: vad ska du göra = what will you do.
gånger i veckan = times per week: fyra gånger i veckan = four times a week.
Many regular verbs form the past with -ade: ritar becomes ritade = drew.
van vid = used to; keep vid before att: van vid att arbeta.
gärna adds a willing, glad tone to a verb: vill gärna prova = would love to try.
Hur är läget is a casual how is it going; läget literally means the situation.
Swedish picks a position verb for location; things lying flat use ligger: segelbåten ligger i hamnen.
